DimensionConstraint.description:
Conventions (normative): angles are CCW from `a` to `b`, reference values reported in [0, 2π); `hDistance`/`vDistance` are signed b − a (with `a === b` = a line: end − start); distances to circles/arcs measure to the curve; `diameter` solves as radius = value / 2.

Dimensions. `driving: true` constrains the solver with `value`; `driving: false` is a reference (driven) dimension whose value is **measured** after solving (planegcs non-driving constraints are unreliable — PLAN §3). `label` positions the text in sketch space for display.

DimensionText.description: Text around a dimension's value. The value itself is never replaceable by text (T1).

count.description: Prefix `N×` with the number of instances (pattern and mirror copies included) of the feature that made `refs[0]`, from `AnnotationResolution.count`; never typed by hand (M4 gate).

precision.description: Decimals; absent = the drawing style's precision. Propagates to every placement.

prefix.description: E.g. `4×`. A hole callout's count is automatic (`HoleCalloutAnnotation.show.count`).

DraftFeature.description: Taper `faces` by `angle` about the `neutral` plane. Each face keeps its line on the neutral plane and turns about it. The pull direction is the neutral plane's normal on the side the drafted faces are; a positive angle makes the body narrower along it (faces lean inward moving away from the neutral plane, as a moulded part needs). Faces centred on the plane use the plane's own normal (a face's outward normal, a plane's +z). `reverse` flips the pull direction.

FeatureFolder.description: A named group of consecutive features in a part's tree (M3.6). UI state such as collapsed is not stored.

features.description: Member feature ids in history order: a contiguous run of `Part.features`. Never empty.

fields.description: Field overrides: JSON pointer inside the feature (e.g. `/end/depth`, `/radius`, `/size`) → value. Only configurable fields are allowed (owner D2: every `Expr` field plus the option fields the document package lists in `CONFIGURABLE_OPTIONS`, e.g. hole size/kind/fit, extrude end kind). An override whose path no longer applies makes that configuration's feature "needs attention", never a silent drop.

propagate.description: M3: extend along tangent-continuous edges (OCCT's behaviour). Default true.

Frame.description: Placement frame: origin plus Z (normal) and X directions. Right-handed; Y = Z × X. Numbers are **millimetres** — the canonical internal length unit for all stored geometry, whatever `WrenDoc.units` says (units only affect display and unit-less expression input). User-editable offsets belong in feature Exprs.

GeometricConstraint.description: Geometric constraints (no value). Ids refer to entities; points are entities too.

appliesTo.description: The size dimension whose feature of size this frame controls (a position frame under `Ø6`): its refs are used and `refs` may be empty. A missing dimension id is needs attention.

diameter.description: Override of the table diameter (drill diameter for tapped holes).

points.description: Sketch points (`S…:p(id)`) or vertices; their sketch must lie on the hole's face.

thread.description: Tapped holes: a cosmetic thread (no helical geometry) over `depth` (default: full).

tipAngle.description: Drill-point cone at a blind end (118° default); omitted = flat bottom.

ImportFeature.description:
A body imported from a file (STEP/IGES/BREP solids, or STL/OBJ/3MF/GLB meshes as reference bodies). The file's bytes live in the project folder at `source.path` (an attachment, e.g. `imports/<featureId>.step`), never inline in the JSON, so documents stay diffable. `sha256` (hex) identifies the bytes for caching and integrity.

Imported faces have no construction history; the regen engine names them `F<id>:face#k` ordered by the deterministic geometric key in naming.ts, and downstream references to them rely on fingerprints when the file is replaced.

frame.description: Placement of the imported geometry (mm); default identity.

LinearDimension.description: Distance between two entities projected on `direction` (unit vector, part coordinates; set by the drawing tool from the view's horizontal or vertical, by promotion from a sketch's u/v). Absent: the natural separation of parallel planes or lines (or a plane and a point); two points without a direction are an `aligned` dimension, and a linear one is flagged "choose a direction". refs: [a, b].

annotations.description: M4 (ADR-081, ADR-090): the part's annotations (annotation.ts): dimensions, GD&T, datums, notes, surface finish, hole callouts. They measure the finished part, so no feature owns them. Absent = none. The array's order carries no meaning: kept sorted by id (store, merge and loader), so concurrent adds never conflict on order.

color.description: CSS hex colour, e.g. `"#9aa4b2"`. Overrides the material's appearance colour.

configurations.description: M3.7 named configurations (ADR-074): sparse overrides over an implicit **Default**, which is the part as stored. Absent = only Default. Keyed by id everywhere, so renames never break merges or consumers. No derived (nested) configurations.

folders.description: Feature tree folders (M3.6, ADR-066). Absent = none. Each folder groups a **contiguous run** of `features` in history order; folders never overlap and do not nest. The array's order carries no meaning (a folder sits in the tree where its first member sits). The document layer keeps the invariant after every edit and merge (`normalizeFolders`): deleted members drop out, empty folders are removed, and members are kept in history order; an edit that would split a run is refused by the command layer (the UI asks first).

material.description: Physical material. Absent = no mass properties beyond volume (UI shows "Assign material").

properties.description: M3.7: the Default configuration's part number and description (and the part's when it has none).

rollbackIndex.description: Features with index >= rollbackIndex are not evaluated. `features.length` = fully rolled forward.

flip.description: Flip the plane normal (and so the sketch's orientation on it).

PushPullFeature.description: Direct editing (PLAN §9.2, M2): moves faces of one body along their normal. Positive `distance` moves outward (adds material), negative inward (removes). M2 supports planar faces; others fail with an `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE` error naming the face. Recorded as a feature, so it is parametric.

suppressed.description: Suppressed annotations are not shown or exported. Per configuration via `AnnotationOverride`.

RefPoint.description: Which point of a referenced entity an annotation measures from (parallel to `refs`). `self`: the entity itself (a face, an edge's line). `center`: circle, arc or sphere centre. `axis`: a cylindrical or conical face's axis; on a planar face in an angle dimension, the face's normal (the pull direction a draft angle is measured from; M4.1). `start` / `end` / `mid`: of an edge. `min` / `max` (M4.1, ADR-095): the entity's extreme point along the dimension's `direction`, only for linear and ordinate dimensions that have one: a circle's, cylinder's or sphere's tangent point, a line's lower or upper end. A diameter in linear form ("across the flats" of a circle) is refs [c, c] at ['min', 'max'].

ShellFeature.description: Hollow a body: remove `openFaces`, offset the rest by `thickness` (inward by default).

openFaces.description: Faces to remove (on one body). Empty = a closed hollow solid.

SketchArc.description: Counter-clockwise from `start` to `end` around `center` (both on the circle).

source.description: M3 Convert Entities: a **linked** entity whose geometry is the projection of model geometry onto the sketch plane, recomputed by the regen engine every time (points, lines, arcs and circles, and since M3.5 ellipses, elliptic arcs and B-splines through the kernel's exact projection; anything else projects as an approximating chain of lines marked `approximate`). Linked entities are fixed (no DOF) and can be dimensioned and constrained to. If `ref` no longer resolves, the sketch is "needs attention" (never re-picked silently). Removing `source` unlinks the entity into ordinary geometry.

SketchBSpline.description: M3.5. A B-spline curve by its control points (`poles`, point entities, so they can be dragged, dimensioned and constrained). Non-periodic splines are clamped: they start at the first pole and end at the last, so a line or arc can share an end point with them. `knots` are distinct values and come with `multiplicities` (both or neither). Omitted: clamped knots i/(n−p) with end multiplicity p + 1 (n poles, degree p), or periodic knots i/n all of multiplicity 1, on the domain [0, 1] (ADR-048 has the periodic flat-knot convention). Explicit knots: end multiplicities must be degree + 1 when not periodic and interior ones ≤ degree; an open spline may instead give a flat knot vector of n + p + 1 values (ADR-048, ADR-056). `weights` omitted = all 1 (non-rational). A spline drawn **through points** stores the poles that interpolate them, plus the through points as point entities held on the curve by `pointOn` constraints, so moving a through point reshapes the curve (ADR-046).

SketchFeature.description: A 2D sketch on a plane or planar face. Geometry and constraints are defined in `sketch.ts`. The kernel turns the solved sketch into wires and regions (names: see `naming.ts`).

on.description: Plane or planar face the sketch lies on (`origin:XY` etc. or a face/plane-feature ref).

visibility.description: Viewport visibility (M3.6). Absent or `'auto'`: shown while no feature uses it, hidden once one consumes it (profile, path, axis; ADR-060). `'shown'` / `'hidden'` override that for this sketch, on every shell, and persist in the document.

SurfaceFinishAnnotation.description: Surface texture symbol (ISO 21920-1 by default). refs: [face].

at.description: Point qualifiers parallel to `refs`; absent or shorter = `'self'` for the rest.

modelPlacement.description: M5 reserve: the v3 `PmiAnnotation.placement` (3D annotation plane and text position), carried over verbatim by the migration so nothing is lost. M5 replaces it with annotation planes.

refs.description:
Model geometry the annotation is attached to, by persistent name (PLAN §7.3). Arity and role per kind are in the .md table ("refs per kind"). Resolved against the part's final state in the view's configuration. Unresolved = needs attention: never re-attached to a guessed entity, and the old value is never displayed (trap T1). Reattach replaces the list (every kind, trap T2). May be empty only where the kind says so (a hole callout bound by `source`, a frame or a datum bound by `appliesTo`).

Construction refs (M4.1, ADR-095), drawn on a view as thin chain lines once a placement there uses them, and offered as pick targets while a picking tool is active: `origin:O`, `origin:X|Y|Z`, `S<id>:p(@origin)`, `S<id>:e(@x|@y)`, `S<id>:p(<point>)`, `F<id>:plane|axis|point`, and `F<pattern>:pitch` (the pitch circle of a circular pattern of holes: about the pattern axis, through the instances' axes; unresolved if they are not holes or not all at one radius, never guessed).

suppressed.description: Suppressed annotations are not shown or exported. Per configuration via `AnnotationOverride`.

SurfaceFinishStandard.description: Surface texture standard (default ISO 21920-1; ISO 1302 is legacy, kept for old drawings).

SurfaceRequirement.description: One surface texture requirement, e.g. `Ra 1.6 µm` (upper limit, `max` rule under ISO 21920).

acceptance.description: Acceptance rule; absent = the standard's default (ISO 21920-1: max; ISO 1302: 16 %).

filter.description: Filter / evaluation length text as written (`0.8`, `λs 2.5 µm`).

parameter.description: Parameter symbol as written by the standard: `Ra`, `Rz`, `Rmr(c)`, `Wt` …

value.description: Length expression; the inline field writes µm (`1.6 µm`).

SweepFeature.description: Sweep closed profile regions along a path (a chain of sketch curves or model edges).

orientation.description: `followPath`: the profile turns with the path (Frenet); `fixed`: it keeps its orientation.

ThreadFeature.description: A cosmetic thread on a cylindrical face: an annotation (drawings, PMI), no geometry change.

Tolerance.description: Tolerance on a dimension's value. Deviations are signed `Expr`s relative to the nominal (so they follow a configuration's nominal). `limits` stores deviations too and is displayed as the two limits. `basic` and `reference` are display forms without a tolerance.

projected.description: Projected tolerance zone Ⓟ with its height.

shape.description: `diameter` = Ø zone, `sphericalDiameter` = SØ; absent = width between two planes/lines.

ZoneModifier.description: Zone modifiers that take no value. Legality per standard is a validation rule, not a type.
